moduleTitle: How to use Hooks in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Recognize when hooks can be used in a test case.
Explain what a Hook is and how it runs relative to a step or a whole test.
Distinguish editor-level Hooks from Configuration File run hooks.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Hooks: running a shared step/group before or after something

elements.description: Test Configuration hooks call an existing shared step/group at configured step/test boundaries. Create or edit the configuration and apply it to the relevant tests; creating a configuration alone does not attach it to every test.

elements.term: Before each step / After each step
elements.description: Per-step handlers attach before/after steps. After handlers have Run on choices (Always, Success, Failure), so they are not unconditional in every configuration. Hooks can still run around a step skipped by its own condition; distinguish that condition from the hook’s Run on selection.

A separate, CLI/config-level mechanism: the Configuration File can define run hooks used to set up the application backend and define parameters before/after a single test or before/after all tests in a run — useful for environment-level setup/teardown that isn't tied to any one specific step.

elements.text: Editor-level Hooks operate at the step/test granularity inside the visual editor; Configuration File hooks operate at the run/suite granularity from the CLI config — both exist so setup/teardown logic doesn't have to be manually duplicated at the start/end of every test.

bulletPoints: Hook = runs a Shared Step/Group before/after a step, or before/after a test.
Per-step hooks observe configured boundaries; after hooks obey their Run on choice.
Configuration File run hooks = backend setup/params before/after a single test, or before/after all tests in a run.
Apply the hook configuration to relevant tests and inspect its results.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: When to recognize a hook is the right tool

elements.title: Common scenarios calling for a hook
items: Setup: configure applicable before-test logic with supported runtime/access and explicit input state.
Per-step observation: collect relevant debugging or intermediate-result evidence without silently repairing an application defect.
Cleanup: configure applicable after-test behavior and verify actual cleanup; hook creation is not a guarantee resources were released.

elements.text: Choose the mechanism for its runtime and lifecycle scope. Shared code reduces duplication, but the hook still requires applicable configuration, dependencies and outcome checks.

bulletPoints: Configure setup and inspect effective state.
Use per-step observation deliberately; avoid masking defects.
Verify cleanup and applicable after-hook Run on behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing an editor Hook with a Configuration File run hook
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming both mechanisms operate at the same level of granularity, or configuring one when the other was needed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Editor Hooks attach a Shared Step/Group before/after a specific step or test inside the visual editor. Configuration File run hooks operate at the CLI/run level, for backend setup and parameters before/after a single test or the whole run.

examPitfalls.title: Manually copying setup/cleanup logic into every test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Re-adding the same 'prepare the environment' steps at the start, and the same 'tear it down' steps at the end, of many separate tests.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use applicable shared setup/cleanup logic with the correct hook mechanism and configuration. Validate resources and Run on behavior; hooking does not itself prove successful cleanup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a Hook in Testim?

options.text: A validation step that only checks API responses.
An object that runs an existing Shared Step or Shared Group before/after each step, or before/after a test.
A tag applied to failed tests for later filtering.
A browser extension used to capture bugs.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's specifically about running something before/after — using existing shared steps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Hook runs an existing Shared Step or Shared Group before/after each step, or before/after a test — not a validation type, a label/tag, or a browser extension.

optionExplanations.A: A hook is a lifecycle mechanism, not only an API response check.
optionExplanations.B: It invokes shared logic at the configured step/test boundary.
optionExplanations.C: Failure tags organize results rather than execute shared hook logic.
optionExplanations.D: Video capture is an extension feature, not a lifecycle hook.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the purpose of Configuration File run hooks, as distinct from editor-level Hooks?

options.text: They are exactly identical to editor Hooks with a different name.
They set up the application backend and define parameters before/after a single test or before/after all tests in a run, from the CLI config.
They only apply to mobile tests.
They replace the need for any Shared Steps.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Configuration File run hooks operate from the CLI config to set up the application backend and define parameters before/after a single test or before/after all tests in a run — a different granularity than editor-level Hooks attached to a specific step or test.

optionExplanations.A: Configuration File hooks and Test Configuration hooks have different mechanisms.
optionExplanations.B: Config hooks support CLI test/suite setup and parameters.
optionExplanations.C: The documented config mechanism is not mobile-only.
optionExplanations.D: Hooks do not remove the need for reusable shared logic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team repeats Node.js database-connection setup before each test in a CLI execution. Which reusable lifecycle mechanism fits this setup?

options.text: A Configuration File beforeTest hook with the required runtime, access and cleanup.
A scenario that has no solution in Testim.
A reason to disable all hooks in the project.
A scenario only solvable by rewriting every test as a custom action.

practiceQuiz.hint: This setup belongs to the stated Node.js CLI execution lifecycle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configuration File beforeTest runs reusable setup for each test in the execution. Configure authorized resource access and verify cleanup; creating an editor configuration alone does not install this Node.js setup.

optionExplanations.A: The config beforeTest lifecycle fits the stated per-test Node.js setup.
optionExplanations.B: Testim provides configuration-file hooks for this setup.
optionExplanations.C: Disabling all hooks does not remove repeated setup.
optionExplanations.D: The entire test need not be rewritten as one custom action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An applied after-each-step hook is configured with Run on Always. Which boundary does it observe, as distinct from afterSuite?

options.text: It runs only once, after the very last step in the test.
It runs after every single step in the test, producing a between-steps effect throughout the run.
It runs only if the test fails.
It has the same effect as a Configuration File's afterSuite hook.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's 'each' step, not just the last one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The per-step handler observes each step boundary under the stated Always setting. Success/Failure settings can restrict other configurations; afterSuite operates on the CLI suite lifecycle.

optionExplanations.A: Once at the suite/test end is different from the stated per-step hook.
optionExplanations.B: Under Always, the applied handler observes each step boundary.
optionExplanations.C: Failure-only is a different Run on selection.
optionExplanations.D: afterSuite operates at the suite lifecycle, not each step.

quickRecap.value: Runs a Shared Step/Group before/after a step, or before/after a test — inside the editor.
Per-step handlers observe configured boundaries; after handlers obey Always/Success/Failure.
